publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Overall, we believe there are many concrete open technical problems relating to accident prevention in machine learning systems.

span.label: accidents in machine learning systems
span.quote: In this paper we discuss one such potential impact: the problem of accidents in machine learning systems, defined as unintended and harmful behavior that may emerge from poor design of real-world AI systems.

span.label: review
span.quote: We review previous work in these areas as well as suggesting research directions with a focus on relevance to cutting-edge AI systems.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AI-safety accidents arise mainly from mis-specified objective functions - negative side effects and reward hacking
span.quote: two broad mechanisms that make it easy to produce wrong objective functions

span.label: The proposed avenues of attack for the wrong-objective problems are explicitly preliminary and not fully worked out.
span.quote: When discussing the problems that arise from having the wrong objective function (reward hacking and side effects, and to a lesser extent scalable supervision), where less prior work exists, our aim is more exploratory—we seek to more clearly define the problem and suggest possible broad avenues of attack, with the understanding that these avenues are preliminary ideas that have not been fully fleshed out.

span.label: The analysis is restricted to RL agents and supervised learning systems rather than all AI paradigms.
span.quote: These are not the only possible paradigms for AI or ML systems, but we believe they are sufficient to illustrate the issues we have in mind, and that similar issues are likely to arise for other kinds of AI systems.

span.label: The multi-agent / rich-modelling route to avoiding side effects is not yet practical.
span.quote: However we are still a long way away from practical systems that can build a rich enough model to avoid undesired side effects in a general sense.

span.label: The review of work relevant to distributional shift is deliberately partial rather than exhaustive.
span.quote: Rather than fully reviewing all of this work in detail (which would necessitate a paper in itself), we will describe a few illustrative approaches and lay out some of their relative strengths and challenges.

span.label: The paper's central term is stipulated so that it attributes a cause, which the ordinary word does not.

span.label: the taxonomy - BY WHERE IN THE PROCESS THINGS WENT WRONG: safety problems are grouped not by the harm produced but by the stage at which the design failed, which is why the five categories are about objectives, oversight and exploration rather than about outcomes
span.quote: We can categorize safety problems according to where in the process things went wrong

span.label: AI safety is framed via accidents — unintended, harmful behavior from poor design — organized into five concrete research problems: avoiding side effects, avoiding reward hacking, scalable supervision, safe exploration, and distributional shift.
span.quote: We present a list of five practical research problems related to accident risk, categorized according to whether the problem originates from having the wrong objective function (“avoiding side effects” and “avoiding reward hacking”), an objective function that is too expensive to evaluate frequently (“scalable supervision”), or undesirable behavior during the learning process (“safe exploration” and “distributional shift”).
